title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-natalie-chen
content:
Notes (scratchpad) — Acme Corp inference contract redline review

Context:
- Customer: Acme Corp (sales rep: Maria Gomez). Private deployment + hosted fallback. Large e-commerce customer; will request data residency in EU region and customer-managed KMS for keys.
- Pricing term under review (Dedicated reserved capacity for baseline + burst). Legal asked for our standard MSA but they pushed back on liability/indemnity and data-use for model improvements.

High-level red flags / clauses to watch:
1) Data use / Model improvements (big red flag)
   - Customer wants explicit prohibition on using their customer data to train or improve public models.
   - Our standard: we may use aggregated/de-identified data to improve the service. Need carveout: exclude PII and customer-specific data; for private/on-prem deployments, commit to no training on their data unless customer opts in and signs data-use addendum.
   - Negotiation talking point: we can accept 'no training' for private deployments + export-control sensitive accounts; agree to a limited telemetry set for performance only (latency/errs) and provide opt-out for telemetry that contains content.

2) IP / Derivative Works
   - Watch for language that claims ownership of customer-generated outputs or derivative works.
   - Propose: customer retains rights to their data and outputs; Redwood retains improvements to platform and underlying models independently developed.

3) Liability / Cap on damages
   - Customer trying to push unlimited liability for certain categories (e.g., data breaches). Standard: liability cap = the greater of (12 months fees) or $1M; carveouts for gross negligence and willful misconduct.
   - Talking point: ask for reasonable cap tied to fees; concede higher cap for severe security breach only if they accept carveouts (no punitive/indirect damages).

4) Indemnity
   - Customer proposes reciprocal indemnities including third-party claims re: outputs. We should limit our indemnity to IP infringement where we control the model code; push back on open-ended indemnities for customer outputs.

5) SLA / Performance Metrics
   - Define measurable metrics: API success rate, p50/p95 latency for inference at X tokens, throughput (tokens/sec) for reserved capacity.
   - Measurement window: monthly rolling; scheduled maintenance excluded (provide schedule).
   - Remedies: service credits up to % of monthly fees. No termination for SLA fail unless repeated breaches (e.g., 3 months below SLA).
   - Talking point: propose 99.9% monthly uptime for hosted API with dedicated capacity targets and explicit CPU/GPU/throughput commitments for Dedicated. Include rollback/canary policy for model version changes with 30-day notice for breaking changes.

6) Data retention & deletion
   - Customer wants immediate deletion on termination plus certification.
   - We should accept deletion and a certificate of deletion for hosted data within 60 days; for private/on-prem, provide deletion procedures and assistance but limited by customer environment.

7) KMS and keys / encryption
   - Customer requires customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM for production. We can offer CMK for hosted enterprise accounts; for Private deployments they keep keys on-prem.

8) Security / Compliance
   - They asked for SOC2 + penetration test reports and right to audit. Provide SOC2 report; limit audit rights to reasonable frequency and scope (e.g., once/year, shared redacted report).

9) Subprocessors / subcontractors
   - They want full list + 30 days notice before adding critical subprocessors. We typically provide categories + notification and escalate major changes.

10) Export control / export of model weights
   - Customer worried about model weights leaving region or being shared. For private deployments we must clarify that we do not export customer-specific models. For hosted API, provide contractual assurances about data residency and no export of customer data.

11) Termination & transition assistance
   - Define transition assistance: data export format, timeframe (30-60 days), costs for extended transition.

12) Confidentiality definition scope
   - Beware overly broad definitions that include anonymized/aggregated data — should be excluded.

13) Insurance
   - Request proof of insurance: general liability, cyber liability. Standard ask: $5M cyber liability. Confirm with finance/legal whether we can accept.

Negotiation posture & fallback positions:
- Data use: accept: (a) hosted: limited telemetry + aggregated/hashed usage for quality improvements; (b) private/on-prem: no training or model improvements w/ customer data without explicit opt-in.
- Liability cap: target = 12 months fees; fallback = 24 months fees for enterprise accounts with higher-tier SLAs.
- SLA: propose service credits only; no termination unless repeated failures.
- Indemnity: limit to IP infringement and to breaches resulting from our gross negligence/willful misconduct.

Practical action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Sync with Solutions Eng (Ryan Murphy) to confirm Dedicated throughput metrics we can commit to (tokens/sec per pod, burst behavior). Link ticket: LEGAL-482.
- [ ] Ask Security for SOC2 + recent pen test summary and redacted report to share with customer (Evelyn to action).
- [ ] Draft data-use addendum that explicitly covers: no-training-for-private, telemetry types collected, deletion timeline. (Jordan to draft initial language).
- [ ] Confirm CMK support and HSM options with infra (ticket: INF-2107).
- [ ] Price team: produce an alternative with higher liability cap and premium for enterprise (Maria in pricing).

Quick negotiation scripts (bullet points to use on calls):
- "We understand your concern about model improvement — for private customers we commit not to use your data to train public models unless you opt in. For hosted customers we only use aggregated, de-identified telemetry; we can provide a log schema and opt-out options."
- "For liability, our standard cap is one year of fees. For enterprise we can discuss an increased cap aligned with committed ARR under a higher support tier."
- "SLA remedies are service credits, not termination rights, unless there are repeated breaches over a prolonged period; that helps us prioritize outages without causing churn risk to either party."

Sample redline language snippets (working):
- Data Use clause: "Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, improve or fine-tune models that are then used to provide services to other customers, except with Customer's prior written consent. Aggregated and de-identified telemetry for service reliability is excluded provided such telemetry cannot be re-identified to Customer or its end-users."

- Deletion clause: "Within sixty (60) days of termination, Provider shall delete or permanently render inaccessible all Customer Data in its systems, and provide a written certification of such deletion upon Customer's request, except to the extent retention is required by law."

- Liability cap: "Except for liability arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence, the aggregate liability of Provider arising under or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer to Provider in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, or (ii) $1,000,000."

Notes-to-self: keep this informal. Save final language into Confluence once we agree on approach.

References / related tickets:
- LEGAL-482: Acme master services negotiation
- INF-2107: CMK/HSM support investigation (Solutions Eng)
- CONFLUENCE: Contract Playbook (link above)

Last thought: for enterprise customers with sensitive data, prefer Private deployments + CMK + contractual ban on training. For hosted-only customers, try to limit telemetry to operational metrics and provide opt-out for content-based telemetry.

-- Natalie
